name: Congenital Hypothyroidism Due to Thyroid Agenesis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Newborn Screening and Confirmatory Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Hypothyroidism

criteria.description: Elevated serum thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels on newborn screening
Low serum free thyroxine (T4) concentration confirming hypothyroidism
Absence of thyroid gland on thyroid ultrasound or radionuclide thyroid scan
Presence of clinical features consistent with hypothyroidism (e.g., prolonged jaundice, feeding difficulties)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Elevated TSH and low free T4 with imaging confirming absent thyroid gland
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Newborn screening programs are critical for early detection; imaging differentiates agenesis from other causes.

pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by ultrasound or radionuclide scan

rare.symptomName: Mental retardation or developmental delay if untreated

imaging: No uptake on radionuclide thyroid scan (e.g., 99mTc-pertechnetate or I-123)
genetic: Mutations rarely identified; mostly sporadic cases
Some familial cases linked to genes involved in thyroid development (e.g., TSHR, PAX8)
other: Newborn screening programs critical for early detection
Response to levothyroxine therapy confirms diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of thyroid gland on imaging
Defects in thyroid hormone synthesis enzymes
Low or normal TSH despite low T4

redFlags: Delayed diagnosis leading to irreversible intellectual disability
Severe hypothyroid symptoms in neonate (e.g., poor feeding, lethargy)
Failure to thrive despite adequate nutrition
references: American Academy of Pediatrics. Clinical Practice Guideline: Screening and Management of Congenital Hypothyroidism. Pediatrics. 2014.
Lazar L, et al. Congenital hypothyroidism due to thyroid dysgenesis: clinical and molecular aspects. Horm Res Paediatr. 2017.
Orphanet: Congenital hypothyroidism due to thyroid agenesis. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2020.
